Rishi / Laura,

Quick follow-up with commercial constraints: Acme is asking to move from 90 -> 60 days for non-renewal. If this is annual and they plan dedicated capacity, that reduces our lead time to reallocate GPUs. For dedicated accounts we typically require 90 days, but for hosted/consumption we can sign to 60 days. Proposal: make notice term conditional in the Order Form — 90 days for Dedicated, 60 days for Hosted.

On termination-for-convenience: commercial is comfortable with a cap equal to unearned prepaid fees plus 30 days of wind-down assistance (at no extra cost) for Hosted. For Dedicated we want either (a) a longer wind-down (90 days) or (b) reimbursement of committed capacity costs (pro-rated) to cover hardware reservation.

I can draft redline language for both scenarios — will have a version by EOD today.

—Kimberly

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — notice windows + termination-for-convenience questions

Maria — thanks for flagging. Attaching proposed redline snippets below and a short rationale.

1) Auto-renew / Notice window: Insert a clause in the Order Form: "Term and Renewal for the Services shall be as set forth in the applicable Order Form. If the Order Form specifies Dedicated Capacity, Customer must provide at least ninety (90) days' written notice prior to the end of the then-current Term to not renew. For non-dedicated (hosted/consumption) Services, Customer must provide at least sixty (60) days' written notice."

Rationale: preserves commercial predictability while letting Hosted customers have shorter notice.

2) Termination for Convenience (Section 7.2): Replace with: "Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. In the event Customer terminates for convenience, Redwood's sole liability shall be (a) refund of any prepaid, unused Fees for Services not yet provided as of the effective termination date, and (b) reasonable assistance for data export for up to thirty (30) days following termination. For Dedicated Capacity where Redwood committed capacity for Customer, Customer shall either (i) reimburse Redwood for committed but unused capacity expenses (pro-rated), or (ii) provide ninety (90) days' notice to avoid a reimbursement obligation."

Rationale: limits downstream liability exposure and ties reimbursement to committed costs for dedicated scenarios.

We'll mark these changes in Acme_MSA_redline_v2.pdf and send the redline back; please confirm commercially which option (reimburse vs. longer notice) Acme prefers for Dedicated.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_clause_snippets.txt]
